evidence.title: Apollonius (freedman)

evidence.title: Apollonius (freedman)
evidence.text: He was a man of great diligence and learning, and anxious to write a history of the exploits of Caesar.

evidence.title: Apollonius (freedman)

evidence.title: Apollonius (freedman)

evidence.title: Apollonius (freedman)
evidence.text: Since he was manumitted as a term of Publius's will, he is by Roman custom likely to have taken the name Publius Licinius Apollonius as a freedman.

evidence.title: Apollonius (freedman)

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Gallienus (c. 218 – September 268), also known as Gallien, was Roman Emperor with his father Valerian from 22 October 253 to spring 260 and alone from spring 260 to September 268.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: He ruled during the Crisis of the Third Century that nearly caused the collapse of the empire.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: While he won a number of military victories, he was unable to prevent the secession of important provinces.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: His 15-year reign was the longest since the 19-year rule of Septimius Severus.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Born into a wealthy and traditional senatorial family, Gallienus was the son of Valerian and Mariniana.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Valerian became Emperor on 22 October 253 and had the Roman senate elevate Gallienus to the ranks of Caesar and Augustus.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Valerian divided the empire between him and his son, with Valerian ruling the east and his son the west.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Gallienus defeated the usurper Ingenuus in 258 and destroyed an Alemanni army at Mediolanum in 259.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: The defeat and capture of Valerian at Edessa in 260 by the Sasanian Empire threw the Roman Empire into the chaos of civil war.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Control of the whole empire passed to Gallienus.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: He defeated the eastern usurpers Macrianus Major and Mussius Aemilianus in 261–262 but failed to stop the formation of the breakaway Gallic Empire under general Postumus.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: Aureolus, another usurper, proclaimed himself emperor in Mediolanum in 268 but was defeated outside the city by Gallienus and besieged inside.

evidence.title: Gallienus
evidence.text: While the siege was ongoing, Gallienus was stabbed to death by the officer Cecropius as part of a conspiracy.

evidence.title: Anne Denman
evidence.text: Anne Denman( 1587–1661) was born in Olde Hall, Retford, Nottinghamshire.

evidence.title: Anne Denman
evidence.text: Through a fortunate second marriage with Thomas Aylesbury, she became the grandmother of Lady Anne Hyde, Duchess of York and great- grandmother of Queen Mary II and Queen Anne.

evidence.title: Hannah Arnold
evidence.text: Hannah Arnold, also known as Hannah Waterman King, was the grandmother of Benedict Arnolds children.

evidence.title: Hubba bint Hulail
evidence.text: Hubba bint Hulail was the grandmother of Hashim ibn' Abd Manaf, thus the great- great- great- grandmother of the Islamic" Nabī"( Prophet) Muhammad ibn Abdullah.

evidence.title: Kaoru Hatoyama
evidence.text: After the elections of 2009, she became more widely known as the grandmother of Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama and his politician brother Kunio Hatoyama.
